newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade inactive-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade inactive-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was near a standstill following active sales this week at $64.00 per cwt, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were light at $64.00, but passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00 to $66.00.
Most feedlots were current, with this week's brisk business moving many showlists, the sources said.

Showlists next week were seen steady to smaller, which could underpin fed cattle prices, or give them a boost, they said. Outlooks for $65.00 fed cattle prices next week were not uncommon among several cattle feeders.
Forecasts for steady to firm prices next week were fortified by ideas boxed beef values would remain strong, the feedlot sources said.
Boxed beef prices at midday were up $0.52 to $0.92 per cwt, with 135 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $104.15, up $0.88 fromThursday's close and up $5.11 since prices started moving higheron July 11, USDA statistics showed.
